outcome: Hemodynamic effects (hypotension, bradycardia, SBP, DBP, MAP)
cohort: The study participants consisted of 50 normotensive ASA grade II parturients and 50 ASA grade III preeclamptic parturients, all planned for LSCS.
finding: Subarachnoid blockade is associated with better perioperative hemodynamic stability and lower risk of hypotension and vasopressor requirements in preeclamptic women compared to healthy subjects.
mod_finding: Subarachnoid block can be safely practiced in preeclamptic patients undergoing caesarean section, offering better perioperative hemodynamic stability and lower vasopressor requirements compared to healthy subjects.
birth_weight: Neonatal weight was measured and found to be comparable between groups (p>0.05), but specific values were not provided.
gest_age: Gestational age was comparable between groups (p<0.05), but specific values were not provided.
